review-lifecycle.exceptions: Further recorded refusal differences (R-PARITY; recorded facts, zero observed harm, no rule): (a) how collection reports a failed round integrity check — both hosts' collect run the check before agreement (reference/review-rules.md#R-AGREE, authoring/shared-dev-log.md DL-52): B's collect re-runs _load_basis/verify_round and raises (bin/review_round_v2.py:508, :532), A's collect runs verify itself before an AGREED record, refuses (exit 2) with one refusal — the round is INVALID, prepare a new round (since triad bb933c6b) — and reports a check that cannot be launched or does not finish as a host fault (exit 64) (lib/collect_v2.py:1555-1582 @ triad ee011968; reference/review-rules.md#R-AGREE); (b) a later edit of the live project roster file — B re-resolves it on every basis load and refuses a difference (bin/review_round_v2.py:121-122), A binds the round's own record and ignores the edit until the next prepare (reference/review-rules.md#R-PREPARE); (c) tampering with recorded attempts outside the threat model — B's sealed terminal refuses changes A's recorded limits (1) and (4) accept (reference/review-rules.md#R-BIND, R-THREAT; D-C66-LIMITS-20261003); (d) how collection reports its outcome (a fact, zero observed harm): On A `review_scratch.py collect` reports the outcome as its exit code: 0 AGREED, 4 BLOCKED, 5 INCOMPLETE; 2 on a refusal; 64 on a host fault. `retry` exits 0 when it allocated, 2 on a refusal and 64 on a host fault (lib/review_scratch.py:5922-5963, lib/collect_v2.py:68-78, :102-112 @ triad e0b15f1). On B `review_round.py v2-collect` prints the canonical result, and its `status` member carries the outcome (INCOMPLETE / BLOCKED / AGREED). The command exits 0 for every outcome and 2 on a refusal (bin/review_round_v2.py:531-534, bin/review_round.py:2436-2452, :2585-2588 @ 7f75863). B's skill reference says to read the outcome from `status`, not the exit code (skills/triad-cross-family-review/references/public-v2-review.md:196-197). R-AGREE records how B's exit 2 mixes host faults with refusals. Retrying an answer that could not be admitted differs by host (recorded difference, zero observed harm, no rule; R-BIND, authoring/shared-dev-log.md DL-55): A treats an attempt sealed invalid as retryable under R-RETRY while its sealed files are unchanged (a changed one is an integrity failure: prepare a new round); B refuses a completed INVALID answer as not a failed-to-run review (bin/review_round_v2.py:345-349, :274-275). A keeps open/touch/close and sibling-resolved helpers moving as one unit; B keeps fingerprint-worktree/render-worktree, guarded-worktree and prepared-directory modes; destructive behavior defined by fences, not a forced rename; no generic `legs` command; candidate collection requires explicit approval of all selected entries without family minimum; B provider-free verification recorded; A verification and host adoption remain separate. Host A has no legacy entry point: the v1 path (`prepare` without `--v2`) and the small path `lib/review_small.py` are removed (triad 12b1dd6f, 32124be5; authoring/shared-dev-log.md DL-59, DL-128). B's legacy entry points (the workspace four-leg gate and the fixed legacy formal route) likewise do not bind the standing review-web authorization — their review_web_authorized is a per-request value, default false (bin/review_round.py:122, :141, :165 @ 7f75863) — a non-conformance fact, R-REVIEW-WEB On B; keeping or retiring them is host B's own decision, DL-59.
